rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado entrepreneurs must make money to spend it as recession talk increases
rows.standfirst: Women entrepreneurs have an answer to a more balanced venture industry. Plus: When local business leaders believe a recession will start, job growth vs. layoffs and more!

rows.title: How a Texas judge’s Affordable Care Act ruling could impact health insurance coverage in Colorado
rows.standfirst: Colorado law protects coverage for preventive services — but that protection doesn’t extend to all insurance plans in the state

rows.title: How to retain resort employees? Colorado ski areas are building workforce housing — at the resorts
rows.standfirst: Like nearly every Colorado ski hill, Winter Park needed big money to help fix its employee housing problem. Enter its deep pocketed operator, Alterra, with a blueprint others can follow.

rows.title: Colorado would offer homeowners, businesses last-resort property insurance under new bill
rows.standfirst: The measure comes in response to growing wildfire risk across the state. The majority of U.S. states already offer state-run or state-regulated property insurance to people who can’t get covered on the private market.

rows.title: Turmoil at Granby Ranch continues as Colorado secretary of state investigates possible metro district board election violations
rows.standfirst: The ski resort operators left. The ski academy plan is done. Residents are suing. Owners are suing. And now the state is looking into claims of election law violations.

rows.title: Denver developer acquires historic resort at Lake Tahoe once owned by Frank Sinatra
rows.standfirst: McWhinney has big plans for Cal Neva Resort & Casino, a historic hotel built along the California-Nevada line in 1926, has been shuttered since 2013

rows.title: How an intergenerational housing development in Montrose aims to improve life for both kids and older adults
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s first intergenerational supportive housing complex is a $10 million bet that a community that feels like family will help ease foster kids’ transition to adulthood.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado moves past bank failures, while startup industry reassesses
rows.standfirst: “Talk to a person, not a building,” says Alpine Bank’s president. Plus: Companies are STILL hiring, reader’s economic outlook, and more!

rows.title: After 50 years, the owner of Beau Jo’s is selling his famous Colorado pizza shop — to his employees
rows.standfirst: Owner Chip Bair said he hopes employee ownership will help ensure the pizzeria’s legacy.

rows.title: So much money, so little of it invested in female founders’ ventures. Colorado entrepreneurs wonder why.
rows.standfirst: While female-founded companies are attracting more venture capital, their share of the pot was 1.9% last year, and has been stuck around 2% for more than a decade.

rows.title: Air emissions, water demands skyrocket as 72% of Colorado’s new oil and gas activity centers on the Front Range
rows.standfirst: Annual state report shows regulators approved 838 new wells in 2022, with a sharp increase on the Front Range

rows.title: In Colorado River talks, still no agreement about water cuts
rows.standfirst: Review pits California and tribal interests against Colorado and five other states that say it’s time to come up with an approach that more fairly shares the river.

rows.title: Colorado planned to lease state land to Utah power company for a natural gas plant. Then protests surfaced.
rows.standfirst: Deseret Power seeks Colorado public land near Rangely for a 50 megawatt generating station, but green groups are attacking the idea of more subsidized fossil fuel burning

rows.title: Why a Colorado switch to cleaner heavy trucks faces big roadblocks
rows.standfirst: State air commission will vote to copy California’s clean trucks mandate, but the trucking industry says no one is ready.

rows.title: Mini hydropower company raises $18M to generate electricity in canals, open assembly facility in Colorado
rows.standfirst: The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation alone operates 1,600 miles of main canals

rows.title: A Durango homeless encampment’s closure left many with nowhere to go. Now, the ACLU is threatening to sue.
rows.standfirst: The shutdown of Purple Cliffs in La Plata County illuminates a city and county’s struggle to adequately serve its homeless population.

rows.title: Five voters will decide billions in Granby Ranch metro-district debt, highlighting calls to reform special tax districts
rows.standfirst: The 24 ballot measures seek approval for a combined $10 billion in debt repayments for each of the five Granby Ranch Metropolitan Districts, none of which have any homes.

rows.title: What’s Working: As home prices drop, Colorado’s real estate industry looks to history to understand trends
rows.standfirst: Plus: Denver-area inflation is up 5.7%, which is higher than the U.S. Some reasons why.

rows.title: Colorado’s increased tobacco taxes are generating more money than expected. State lawmakers want to keep the surplus.
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1290 would refer a question to the November ballot requesting that the extra money collected through Proposition EE be transferred to Colorado’s new universal preschool program and the legislature’s general fund

rows.title: What Coloradans need to know about renewing Medicaid as many face losing their coverage
rows.standfirst: As many as 325,000 people could lose Medicaid coverage in Colorado over the coming year. This guide will tell you how to navigate that.

rows.title: Lo que los coloradenses necesitan saber para renovar Medicaid ya que muchos podrían perder su cobertura
rows.standfirst: Hasta 325,000 personas podrían perder su cobertura de Medicaid en Colorado a lo largo del año que viene. Esta guía te dirá cómo guiarte por el proceso de renovación.

rows.title: The Colorado Sun isn’t robocalling you. Here’s what to do if you get a call.
rows.standfirst: Get a robocall from a Colorado Sun selling solar panels? It’s not from us. Here are some ways to make the calls stop

rows.title: Housing density requirements dramatically pared back in Colorado governor’s major land-use use bill
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 213 was amended Tuesday to build more support for the measure among lawmakers and to ensure the legislation’s passage out of its first committee

rows.title: More than 100 homes are still uninhabitable from Marshall fire smoke and ash contamination
rows.standfirst: Marshall fire survivors with homes still standing continue to face unique hurdles more than a year later

rows.title: State lawmakers introduce big measure attempting to rein in Coloradans’ utility bills. Here’s what it does.
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 291 aims to prevent big spikes in electric and gas bills due to gas market volatility, which can be cause by a winter freeze in Texas or a war in Ukraine, while also trying to limit what costs utilities like Xcel Energy can pass onto consumers

rows.title: Housing, energy and food costs push Denver’s inflation higher than the national rate
rows.standfirst: The Denver-area’s inflation rate was 5.7% in March compared to the 5% national rate.

rows.title: First audit of Denver’s response to unauthorized encampments finds the city is mostly — but not fully — compliant
rows.standfirst: The city appears to equitably provide services, conduct assessments and perform cleanups. But it needs to do more to ensure people have access to their belongings.

rows.title: Colorado’s effort to attract more federal broadband funding seems to be working
rows.standfirst: After challenging thousands of incorrect data points on a national map, Colorado stands to gain millions of dollars more in federal funding

rows.title: Ganja glut? With excess cannabis, growers seek interstate sales
rows.standfirst: Twenty-one states have now legalized the recreational use of cannabis by adults

rows.title: What’s Working: When the CHIPS Act, education and jobs come together in Colorado
rows.standfirst: The CHIPS Act rewards chipmakers that bring manufacturing back to the U.S. Colorado’s 2.8% unemployment rate, starter homes and more!

rows.title: Denver’s first Native American affordable housing project aims to make amends for U.S. policy
rows.standfirst: The 187-unit apartment building with a symbolic circular design will include an Indian Health Services clinic and cultural programming in Denver.

rows.title: Colorado greenlights California-style clean trucks mandate in air pollution fight
rows.standfirst: Dealers must add clean electric medium and heavy trucks for ‘27 model year, and switch to low-NOx scores in fossil fuel engines

rows.title: 5 years in, Opportunity Zone investments in Colorado are yielding important dividends
rows.standfirst: Ranked second in the nation for program success, Colorado is a billion dollars richer in projects, with rural towns and cities both reaping the bounty

rows.title: Major land-use bill from Colorado governor, Democrats is gutted to remove all upzoning requirements
rows.standfirst: A 39-page amendment adopted Wednesday was aimed at winning over skeptics of Senate Bill 213, the cornerstone of Democrats’ affordable housing efforts in the legislature this year

rows.title: Colorado’s ban on cities, counties enacting rent control will remain in place
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1115, which would have repealed the prohibition, was rejected after a Democratic lawmaker joined Republicans in a Colorado Senate committee in voting against the measure

rows.title: Denver-area assessors warn of major spike in property taxes as Colorado legislature rushes to provide relief
rows.standfirst: In Douglas County, assessed home values, used to calculate property taxes, increased by as much as 50%. In Denver, officials say the median increase is 33%.

rows.title: MoonBikes are a battery-powered snowmobile alternative for dashing through the Colorado snow
rows.standfirst: The French snowbikes could lure winter travelers with a quieter, more sustainable option for scooting over snow. They’re a new challenge for land managers handling next-gen motorized travel.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado women earned 85.4 cents for every dollar a man made in 2021
rows.standfirst: It was even worse in the pandemic. Plus: CSU’s economic forecast for the state, daily paychecks and it’s National Small Business Week!
